key_points.description: Meeting purpose: review and clarify open SOW questions between Dataskate and AGRODeviate ahead of project kickoff.
Scope clarification on item one confirmed — if a feature already works, it's out of scope; if it doesn't, it's in scope.
25-hour Salesforce buffer covers all changes required to make the scoped use cases functional, regardless of whether it hits exactly 25 or 30 hours.
Salesforce health check is in scope — Dataskate will assess standard features not being used and recommend fixes; items fixable within roughly two days' effort will be implemented at no extra charge.
Dashboard rework was not explicitly scoped, but can be prioritized within the 25-hour buffer after the health check assessment.
Error handling for QuickBooks downtime will use email notifications; once QuickBooks is back online, processing resumes and no data loss is expected.
New ship-to and bill-to addresses will be pushed to QuickBooks as part of order creation, not as standalone syncs.

New part numbers mid-year can be auto-created in QuickBooks when first included in an order; however, inventory quantity defaults need clarification since inventory is managed in Mysis, not QuickBooks.

Pricing and product descriptions will not auto-sync — annual price book updates require manual maintenance in both Salesforce and QuickBooks; new parts added mid-year via orders will update QuickBooks from that point forward.

Back-order handling discussed — preferred approach is to split orders in Salesforce by available vs. unavailable inventory, with an override option or ship-date delay to keep items on a single order when stock is due imminently.

Packing slip generation is in scope as a reference sync, but auto-triggering the print from QuickBooks Desktop needs further research; generating the slip natively in Salesforce would be additional out-of-scope work.
Post-go-live warranty support covers 15 days; issues arising after that require either a managed services agreement or a purchased bucket of hours.

UAT responsibility falls on AGRODeviate, who must create test cases covering scenarios like new part numbers, new ship-to addresses, partial shipments, and back orders; Dataskate will fix any failures found during testing.
Second payment milestone agreed — AGRODeviate needs to visually confirm data moving between systems across use cases one through five, not necessarily full completion.
Team access setup: Dataskate will provide names and email addresses of project team members (based in India) so AGRODeviate's IT group can configure VPN access before the kickoff call.

data.raw_content:
## Action Items
- [ ]  Kailash to add a clarifying point to the SOW about the 25-hour scope covering Salesforce health check and improvements.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Kailash to check with his Salesforce architect about a faster way to create orders without requiring an opportunity.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Kailash to research whether QuickBooks Desktop supports automatic packing slip generation via API when an order is created.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Kailash to collect team member names and email addresses from the project management team and send them to Doug for VPN/environment access setup.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  douge@agrodeviate.com to follow up with Jackson to confirm procurement of the test environment license. 

## Key Points
- Meeting purpose: review and clarify open SOW questions between Dataskate and AGRODeviate ahead of project kickoff. 
- Scope clarification on item one confirmed — if a feature already works, it's out of scope; if it doesn't, it's in scope. 
- 25-hour Salesforce buffer covers all changes required to make the scoped use cases functional, regardless of whether it hits exactly 25 or 30 hours. 
- Salesforce health check is in scope — Dataskate will assess standard features not being used and recommend fixes; items fixable within roughly two days' effort will be implemented at no extra charge. 
- Dashboard rework was not explicitly scoped, but can be prioritized within the 25-hour buffer after the health check assessment. 
- Error handling for QuickBooks downtime will use email notifications; once QuickBooks is back online, processing resumes and no data loss is expected. 
- New ship-to and bill-to addresses will be pushed to QuickBooks as part of order creation, not as standalone syncs. 
- New part numbers mid-year can be auto-created in QuickBooks when first included in an order; however, inventory quantity defaults need clarification since inventory is managed in Mysis, not QuickBooks. 
- Pricing and product descriptions will not auto-sync — annual price book updates require manual maintenance in both Salesforce and QuickBooks; new parts added mid-year via orders will update QuickBooks from that point forward. 
- Back-order handling discussed — preferred approach is to split orders in Salesforce by available vs. unavailable inventory, with an override option or ship-date delay to keep items on a single order when stock is due imminently. 
- Packing slip generation is in scope as a reference sync, but auto-triggering the print from QuickBooks Desktop needs further research; generating the slip natively in Salesforce would be additional out-of-scope work. 
- Post-go-live warranty support covers 15 days; issues arising after that require either a managed services agreement or a purchased bucket of hours. 
- UAT responsibility falls on AGRODeviate, who must create test cases covering scenarios like new part numbers, new ship-to addresses, partial shipments, and back orders; Dataskate will fix any failures found during testing. 
- Second payment milestone agreed — AGRODeviate needs to visually confirm data moving between systems across use cases one through five, not necessarily full completion. 
- Team access setup: Dataskate will provide names and email addresses of project team members (based in India) so AGRODeviate's IT group can configure VPN access before the kickoff call.
